summary: Created user datauser on node1 and provisioned /srv/data as its own 100MB ext4 loopback filesystem (backed by /srv/datauser.img, mounted via /etc/fstab), owned exclusively by datauser. The 100MB cap is enforced by the filesystem itself: writes beyond ~86MB usable space fail with ENOSPC. Verified enforcement both before and after a full node restart (boot_id changed, confirming a real reboot), and confirmed the mount, ownership, and quota enforcement all survive persistently.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 16.04, single ext4 root filesystem (/dev/vda1), no existing /srv/data, no datauser account, no quota tooling installed
Created system user datauser (useradd -m, nologin shell)
Created a 100MB file /srv/datauser.img, formatted it ext4, mounted it at /srv/data with -o loop
Set ownership of /srv/data to datauser:datauser, mode 700
Verified as datauser: writing 200MB into /srv/data fails with ENOSPC at ~86MB (filesystem-enforced), confirmed df shows 100% used
Cleaned up test file, unmounted/remounted via fstab entry to confirm persistence of mount, ownership, and permissions
Captured baseline boot_id and healthy state (mount, ownership, quota enforcement) before restart
Issued backgrounded shutdown -r now on node1 so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot_id proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: verified /srv/data auto-mounted via fstab, ownership intact, and re-tested that datauser still hits ENOSPC at ~86MB, confirming quota enforcement persisted across reboot

evidence.summary: useradd for datauser succeeded via sudo; id datauser confirms uid=1001(datauser)

evidence.requirement: /srv/data limited to 100MB, enforced by the filesystem
evidence.summary: 100MB image created, ext4-formatted, mounted at /srv/data; write test as datauser of 200MB fails with ENOSPC at 84-86MB, df shows 100% used on the /dev/loop0 93M filesystem

evidence.requirement: Enforcement is by the filesystem itself, not application-level, and persists across remounts
evidence.summary: Added /etc/fstab entry for the loop mount; umount/mount cycle shows the same 93M filesystem remounts with correct ownership

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 6ab98831-2739-47d3-b99c-0784ebb8b49e plus healthy mount/ownership/quota state before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded shutdown -r now returned REBOOT_ACK immediately; subsequent poll got connection refused, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is f4b9c173-cdd7-4319-964f-f5ef5f8c2a6a, differing from the pre-restart value, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required state (mount, ownership, quota enforcement)
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/data auto-mounted via fstab with correct ownership; datauser write test again hit ENOSPC at ~86MB confirming the 100MB filesystem-enforced limit survived the reboot
